questions.question: What is blood classified as?
questions.solution_html:
• What is blood classified as? /
  • Ans: Blood is classified as a connective tissue because it connects different parts of the body by
  • transporting oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products. It consists of two main components:
  • plasma (the liquid part) and formed elements (red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets). Although
  • it is a fluid, it performs the same functions as other connective tissues —binding and supporting body
  • structures.

questions.final_answer: structures.

questions.question: Explain the structure and functions of the heart with a neat diagram.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the structure and functions of the heart with a neat diagram. /
  • Ans: Structure:
  • • The heart is a muscular, cone-shaped organ located in the thoracic cavity, between the lungs.
  • • It is made of cardiac muscle and is divided into four chambers:
  • • Right atrium and right ventricle (receive and pump deoxygenated blood)
  • • Left atrium and left ventricle (receive and pump oxygenated blood)
  • • Valves (tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic) ensure one-way flow of blood.
  • • The septum divides the heart into right and left sides.
  • • The heart is enclosed in a protective sac called the pericardium.
  • Functions:
  • • Pumping Blood: The heart acts as a pump to circulate blood throughout the body.
  • • Oxygen Transport: It sends deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation and oxygenated
  • blood to the body.
  • • Maintains Blood Pressure: Regular contractions maintain proper blood pressure and flow.
  • • Removes Waste: It helps transport carbon dioxide and other waste products for elimination.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: • Removes Waste: It helps transport carbon dioxide and other waste products for elimination.

questions.question: Explain the role of the spinal cord in reflex action and communication.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of the spinal cord in reflex action and communication. /
  • Ans: 1. In Reflex Action:
  • • The spinal cord acts as the center for reflexes.
  • • During a reflex action (like pulling your hand away from a hot object), the sensory neurons
  • carry impulses from receptors to the spinal cord.
  • • The spinal cord quickly processes this information through interneurons and sends a response
  • through motor neurons to the muscles — without involving the brain.
  • • This allows the body to respond rapidly to danger or stimuli.
  • • Example: Touching something hot → sensory impulse to spinal cord → motor impulse to hand
  • muscles → hand withdraws.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: muscles → hand withdraws.

questions.question: Discuss the structural features and functions of neutrophils.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the structural features and functions of neutrophils. /
  • Ans: 1. Structural Features:
  • • Type: Neutrophils are a type of white blood cell (WBC), specifically granulocytes.
  • • Nucleus: They have a multi -lobed nucleus (usually 2 –5 lobes), which gives them the name
  • polymorphonuclear leukocytes.
  • • Cytoplasm: The cytoplasm contains fine granules that stain lightly with both acidic and basic
  • dyes (hence the name neutrophil).
  • • Size: They are about 10–12 micrometers in diameter.
  • • Mobility: Neutrophils are highly motile and can move through capillary walls into tissues by
  • diapedesis.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: diapedesis.

questions.question: Explain bone remodeling and factors that influence it
questions.solution_html:
• Explain bone remodeling and factors that influence it /
  • Ans: Bone remodeling is the continuous process of breaking down old bone tissue and forming new
  • bone tissue to maintain bone strength and mineral balance. It helps in repairing micro -damages,
  • reshaping bones after stress, and regulating calcium levels in the blood.
  • Steps in Bone Remodeling:
  • • Resorption: Osteoclasts break down and remove old or damaged bone tissue.
  • • Reversal: The bone surface is prepared for new bone formation.
  • • Formation: Osteoblasts build new bone matrix and deposit minerals.
  • • Resting phase: The new bone becomes mature and remains until the next remodeling cycle.
  • Factors Influencing Bone Remodeling:
  • • Hormones – Parathyroid hormone (PTH), calcitonin, growth hormone, and sex hormones
  • (estrogen, testosterone) regulate bone resorption and formation.
  • • Mechanical stress or exercise – Physical activity and weight-bearing exercise strengthen bones
  • by stimulating bone formation.
  • • Nutrition – Adequate calcium, vitamin D, and protein are essential for bone health.
  • • Age – Remodeling slows with age, leading to bone loss.
  • • Genetics – Determines bone density and structure.
  • • Diseases and medications – Conditions like osteoporosis or drugs such as steroids can affect
  • remodeling.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: remodeling.

questions.solution_html:
• Explain irritability in muscles and its importance for survival. /
  • x4 = 20]
  • Ans: Irritability (also called excitability) is the ability of a muscle or nerve tissue to respond to a
  • stimulus, usually a nerve impulse (such as an electrical or chemical signal). It is one of the essential
  • properties of living tissues, especially in muscles and nerves.
  • When stimulated, the muscle generates an electrical signal that leads to contraction.
  • Explanation:
  • Muscles receive signals from the nervous system through motor neurons.
  • These signals (stimuli) cause chemical and electrical changes in the muscle fibers. This leads to muscle
  • contraction, enabling movement or other vital functions (like heartbeat or breathing).
